title: Shakuntala
subtitle: From the Mahabharata and Kalidasa's play

intro.title: A girl raised by the forest
intro.body:
Long ago, the sage Vishwamitra sat so deep in meditation that the gods in heaven grew afraid of his power. Indra sent the apsara Menaka down to break his concentration, and she did. From their love a daughter was born.

This is the story of that daughter: how she was found, how she fell in love with a king and was forgotten by him, and how a lost ring and a fearless child brought them back together.

characters.name: Shakuntala
characters.epithet: Daughter of a sage and an apsara
characters.blurb: Abandoned at birth and raised in the sage Kanva's forest hermitage, she grew up among deer, birds and flowering trees. She is gentle but proud, and she will not beg anyone to believe the truth.

characters.name: Dushyanta
characters.blurb: A brave and handsome king who strays into the hermitage while hunting a deer. He loves quickly and sincerely, but a curse will steal his memory of her.

image.caption: King Dushyanta (detail, cropped)
image.credit: After Raja Ravi Varma (1848-1906); Wellcome Collection

characters.name: Kanva
characters.blurb: A wise old sage who found a baby guarded by birds and raised her as his own daughter. He named her Shakuntala: the one protected by birds.

characters.name: Menaka
characters.blurb: The most beautiful of the celestial dancers. She was sent to earth on a mission and had to leave her daughter behind when she returned to heaven.

characters.name: Vishwamitra
characters.epithet: A king who became a great sage
characters.blurb: Once a warrior king, he gave up his throne to seek spiritual power. His meditation was so fierce that even Indra feared him.

characters.name: Anasuya
characters.blurb: The thoughtful one of Shakuntala's two closest friends in the hermitage. She notices everything and worries about what might go wrong.

characters.name: Priyamvada
characters.blurb: The playful one of the pair, always teasing. Her name means 'she who speaks sweetly', and her words calm even an angry sage.

characters.name: Durvasa
characters.blurb: A powerful sage famous for his curses. Anyone who fails to honour him had better beware.

characters.name: Bharata
characters.blurb: Born and raised in a forest hermitage, he is afraid of nothing, not even lions. He will grow up to be an emperor, and India, Bharat, will carry his name.

events.title: Born of Earth and Heaven
events.setup: Menaka must return to heaven. What will become of the baby?

image.caption: Vishwamitra refuses the child Menaka offers him

dialogue.speaker: menaka
dialogue.text: She is your daughter too. Take her!

dialogue.speaker: vishwamitra
dialogue.text: I have already given up too much for you. Go!
The baby was left by a river, where birds sheltered her with their wings.

payoff.title: Protected by birds
payoff.body:
Neither parent could keep the child. Vishwamitra turned back to his meditation, and Menaka returned to heaven.

The sage Kanva found the baby beside the river Malini, guarded by a ring of birds. He named her Shakuntala, 'the one protected by birds', and raised her as his own.

events.title: The Glance Back
events.setup: A king chasing a deer wanders into the hermitage, and Shakuntala sees him.

image.caption: Shakuntala pretends to pull a thorn from her foot so she can look back

dialogue.speaker: priyamvada
dialogue.text: Why have you stopped, Shakuntala?

dialogue.speaker: shakuntala
dialogue.text: A thorn... in my foot.

dialogue.speaker: shakuntala
dialogue.text: Just one more look at him.

payoff.title: Two worlds meet
payoff.body:
King Dushyanta had followed a deer deep into the forest and stopped his chariot at Kanva's hermitage out of respect. There he saw Shakuntala watering the plants with her friends.

Neither of them said much. But as she walked away, she stopped, pretended a thorn had caught her foot, and looked back.

events.title: A Letter on a Lotus Leaf
events.setup: Shakuntala cannot eat or sleep. Her friends know exactly why.

image.caption: Shakuntala writes a love letter to Dushyanta

dialogue.speaker: anasuya
dialogue.text: Write to him. Tell him what you feel.

dialogue.speaker: shakuntala
dialogue.text: What if a king does not care for a forest girl?

dialogue.speaker: priyamvada
dialogue.text: Use your fingernail on the lotus leaf. We'll deliver it!

payoff.title: Words scratched with a fingernail
payoff.body:
With no ink and no paper in the hermitage, Shakuntala scratched her feelings onto a soft lotus leaf with her fingernail.

Dushyanta was hiding nearby, listening. He stepped out before the letter could ever be sent.

events.title: The Ring
events.setup: While Kanva is away, the king and Shakuntala make a promise.

image.caption: King Dushyanta gives Shakuntala his ring
image.credit: After Raja Ravi Varma (1848-1906); Wellcome Collection

dialogue.speaker: dushyanta
dialogue.text: Wear my signet ring. Count one letter of my name each day, and before you reach the end, I will send for you.

dialogue.speaker: shakuntala
dialogue.text: I will count every one.

payoff.title: A marriage of the heart
payoff.body:
They married by the Gandharva rite, a marriage of mutual love with no priest and no guests, only the forest as witness.

Then duty called the king back to his capital. He left Shakuntala his royal ring as a promise.

events.title: The Curse of Durvasa
events.setup: Shakuntala is dreaming of her husband, so deeply that she does not hear a guest at the gate.

dialogue.speaker: durvasa
dialogue.text: You ignore a sage at your door? Then the one you dream of will forget you!

dialogue.speaker: priyamvada
dialogue.text: Forgive her, great one! She meant no insult.

dialogue.speaker: durvasa
dialogue.text: A curse cannot be undone. But if he sees a token he gave her, he will remember.

payoff.title: A curse, and a way out
payoff.body:
The fiery sage Durvasa cursed Shakuntala for failing to greet him. Her friends begged for mercy, and he softened the curse: the king would remember her if he saw a token he had given her.

The friends never told Shakuntala. After all, she had the ring. When Kanva returned and learned of the marriage, he blessed her and sent her to her husband's court.

events.title: Forgotten
events.setup: Shakuntala stands before the king's throne. He looks at her like a stranger.

image.caption: Shakuntala in the court of Dushyanta

dialogue.speaker: dushyanta
dialogue.text: I have never seen this woman before.

dialogue.speaker: shakuntala
dialogue.text: Then look at your own ring!
But her finger was bare. The ring had slipped off while she bathed in a sacred river.

payoff.title: The ring in the river
payoff.body:
On the journey to the capital, Shakuntala had stopped to offer prayers at a river, and the loose ring slipped from her finger into the water.

With no token to break the curse, the king remembered nothing. The court turned its back on her.

events.title: Carried Away
events.setup: Rejected and alone, Shakuntala cries out. Someone in heaven hears her.

dialogue.speaker: shakuntala
dialogue.text: Mother Earth, open and take me in!

dialogue.speaker: menaka
dialogue.text: Hush, my daughter. You will not be alone again.

payoff.title: A mother returns
payoff.body:
A flash of light, and Shakuntala was gone. Her mother Menaka had come for her at last, and carried her to the peaceful hermitage of the sage Marica, high in the Himalayas.

There, far from any court, her son was born.

events.title: The Boy Who Counted a Lion's Teeth
events.setup: Years pass. In a mountain hermitage, a small boy has caught something dangerous.

image.caption: Young Bharata with a lion cub

dialogue.speaker: bharata
dialogue.text: Open your mouth, little lion! I want to count your teeth!
Behind the rocks, the lioness was watching.

payoff.title: Sarvadamana, the tamer of all
payoff.body:
The hermits called the boy Sarvadamana, 'the one who tames everything', because he wrestled lion cubs and was afraid of nothing.

Meanwhile, far away, a fisherman cut open a fish and found a royal ring inside. When the king saw it, the curse broke, and his memory of Shakuntala came flooding back, along with bitter regret.

events.title: Recognised
events.setup: Returning from a battle for the gods, the king stops at a mountain hermitage and meets a fearless boy.

image.caption: Dushyanta kneels before his son, with Shakuntala

dialogue.speaker: bharata
dialogue.text: Mother, who is this man?

dialogue.speaker: dushyanta
dialogue.text: Shakuntala... can you forgive me?

dialogue.speaker: shakuntala
dialogue.text: It was the curse, not his heart.

payoff.title: A family made whole
payoff.body:
The boy's protective amulet, which only his parents could touch, lay in the king's hand without harm. Dushyanta knew then that this was his son.

Shakuntala forgave him. The three of them returned to the capital together.

finale.title: Why this story survived
finale.body:
The boy grew up to be Emperor Bharata, and India's own name for itself, Bharat, is said to come from him. The Mahabharata tells the story of his descendants.

Centuries later the poet Kalidasa retold it as a play, adding the ring, the curse and the fish. It became one of the best-loved works of Sanskrit literature, and when it was translated into European languages in the 1790s, Goethe wrote that heaven and earth were contained in that one name, Shakuntala.
